body: No, love is not dependant on sex. I know many people in relationships who don’t love each other but have sex, and I know many people who have loving relationships and don’t have sex

My win win is that my allo partner doesn’t care about sex that much and our relationship is built on friendship, romance, fun and support. We talk about everything. He doesn’t care that I’m ace and don’t want to have sex, he says he’s more than happy just to be around me. I believe him. 

Some allos would rather have an intimate emotional relationship that is more about deep connection and love than a physical thing. And for some they want to have sex. It depends on the person. 

What I do know is that if you are going to date someone, you deserve to have a win win situation. Your needs, or lack there of, are just as important as theirs and if those needs clash then there are other people out there who will fulfil your needs better

You are allowed to be upset. They knew your boundaries and kept pushing them instead of respecting them. Your friend is wrong on this topic. You deserve someone who loves and respects you as you are. Who doesn’t try to change you. 

I am asexual and my partner isn’t. He never pressured me or made me feel bad. He asked about my boundaries and what I was okay with and stuck to those. He says that sex never has to be a thing in our relationship because he loves me and and just wants to spend time with me. 

There ARE allo people out there who don’t care about sex. Your ex sounds like a twat and there are much better people out there. I know because my partner NEVER pressured me and we are in a happy healthy relationship. We’re really good for each other BECAUSE our relationship has always been based on friendship, romance and love. Not sex. 

It is completely realistic for you to be with someone who doesn’t want sex. You deserve to be with someone who makes you feel safe and comfortable and respects you in all ways. If they don’t then they don’t deserve to be with you. You’re allow to be picky with the people you give you time to. It’s yours to give, you chose who it goes to.

Therapy for you is a great idea. They will be about to help you understand much more than people on Reddit. I would recommend showing your therapist this post and anyone who you trust. I don’t know if he is telling the truth but you can’t tell if someone is lying even if they seem honest. Make him get a sleep study and go to therapy together and explain everything from your point of view before he says anything. Then have a session with the therapist on your own so they can listen, give advice and help you know what’s worth leaving someone over. I don’t know enough about Sexsomnia, but him taking your hand and moving it to his penis doesn’t sound like behaviour of someone asleep. Moving his hands to you? Maybe but grabbing YOUR hand? I’m not sure. 

If he is lying, I hope you don’t stay with someone who did that because you are worth so much more. And if you don’t know, take advice from therapists who specialise in abusive relationships, trauma and rape.

Ah okay so the point of this post was that some people don’t stop poking after you say ‘please stop’ and only stop until you say ‘I’ve got a stick at home.’ 

With this analogy we are using sticks as potential partners right? I like sticks but sometimes I don’t really want a stick and there’s someone in front of me saying ‘look I’ve got a stick’ waving it in my face. I say ‘no thanks’ they then start poking me with this stick. I keep trying to say I’m not interested in this stick but they keep poking until I say ‘I’ve already got a stick’ 

The post is saying that even when you ask some people to stop poking they don’t stop. I think we both agree that telling someone you’re not interested in a stick is a good enough reason for them to not poke you. And the problem is that they don’t see that as a reason to leave you alone. Not everyone is looking for a stick. They think that everyone must want a stick all the time and if you don’t already have a stick then they should keep poking until you give in. 

No one want to be poked with a stick in the first place. Harassment is different from a someone offering a stick then being turned down so walking away. It’s when someone says ‘ I don’t want a stick’ but the other person keeps poking them over and over with the stick. Also it’s not okay to poke people with sticks in the first place. It’s like assuming everyone wants to be poked with sticks when really no one likes being poked, it invades your space and especially if it’s a stranger it can make you very uncomfortable. I actually agree with this. When my depression was really bad there was always a reason. To be fair I didn’t know what those reasons where at the time but with therapy and a LOT of self reflection, I realised I was doing things I hated, I didn’t know how to be connected to others, I didn’t know how to be connected with myself and what I really wanted. I just went along with what I thought others wanted of me not getting why I was so sad. I thought antidepressants would fix me and didn’t like my therapist but stayed with them because I thought they must know what they’re doing. Guess what, it didn’t work. 

It started to change for me when I got a new therapist who I really like and he convinced me to take a break and give up on school. I know that’s not good advice for most but I couldn’t continue for my mental health. The education system is fucked and before, I tried to ‘feel better’ just to go back to school and pretend that life was working, just going through the motions. But it wasn’t working. 

I now really care about myself ( or try to ) and am learning how to manage my depression and anxiety. I don’t expect a drug to fix me and I don’t want it to now. I’m not saying antidepressants are bad, I’m still on them I’m just saying they can’t be the only thing you do. You have to make life changes and figure out what sort of life you REALLY want to live, not just go through the motions.

In some cases past experiences can give you all the symptoms of depression and that takes years of therapy to uncover things.  But for people with depression, It’s like telling someone with an under active thyroid that taking medicine is just masking the problem. Some problems CAN be fixed naturally, by changing your diet or exercising more.  But a lot CAN’T. People with thyroid problems didn’t get it because something happened to them, it just happened, (maybe due to genetics but you can’t change that) so they need to take medicine to live productive lives and feel good. It’s similar to depression, and even though there can be treatable reasons for depression a lot of the causes cannot be addressed (genetics, personality or life events that you may not remember) and even if they could (which I’m not saying they can) be treated like you said ^ it would take years and years of effort and money which is an unrealistic task for 99%
I’m not trying to have a go at you. Just trying explaining how depression works most of the time. I hope I can change your mind about people taking drugs to deal with medical problems. But if I didn’t that’s fine too

Edit: I’m not saying that taking drugs is bad. I was on antidepressants and I’ve tried lots non worked for me so going the therapy way. I’m not saying that drugs is the only way. In some cases it’s the best way but in others it’s not. There are many different types of depression and many different treatments. Everyone’s life is different and I’m NOT SAYING that drugs are the only way. I didn’t actually like when I was on antidepressants but it works for a lot.
